priorityActions: Activate emergency response and prepare for/assist with immediate pericardiocentesis by the experienced drainage team.
Administer a rapid isotonic IV fluid bolus as prescribed to support preload and perfusion while awaiting definitive drainage.
reasoning: The enlarging effusion, obstructive-shock findings, elevated jugular venous pressure, and echocardiographic diastolic chamber collapse identify cardiac tamponade. Definitive treatment is urgent pericardial drainage; isotonic fluid can temporarily support preload while drainage is arranged. Improving arterial pressure and falling jugular venous pressure indicate restoration of cardiac filling and perfusion.
